definition.|S|: candidates whose verdict is engine_alive/executed; unknown and engine_death are never members (contracts.safe_action_set)

discriminating.definition: a state is discriminating when 0 < |S| < 18 and every one of its 18 arms carries a valid verdict (fail-closed: any unknown arm disqualifies the state from this count)
discriminating.raw_note: the raw count would accept a state with an unknown arm; it is reported only so a reader can see the fail-closed rule changed nothing (or what it changed)

proper.definition: 0 < |S| < 18 with all 18 arms carrying a valid verdict and no prefix HASH mismatch (the fail-closed proper count)

rule.order: the 200 states are built by the plan phase in this fixed order: for each TRAIN seed in seed_source.seeds (3042..3091, ascending), for each offset in offsets (30, 60, 90, 120, ascending), one state at floor_to_2(first_death_frame(seed) - offset); state index = seed_index * 4 + offset_index, so index 0 is (3042, offset 30) and index 199 is (3091, offset 120)
rule.stratum_names: train_proximate_offset30 / _offset60 / _offset90 / _offset120 - four strata of 50 states each, so every per-offset rate has denominator 50
rule.floor: every state frame is floored to the 2-frame decision grid (floor_to_2); the actual offset recorded per state (death_frame - decision_frame) is therefore the nominal offset or one frame more
rule.dedup: no two states of this pass share (seed, decision_frame); the plan refuses a duplicate instead of silently dropping one
rule.fallback: there is no fallback in this pass. A seed whose probe records no first death within probe.max_frames, or whose floored proximate frame would be < 40 or beyond the recorded trace, is a hard failure: the plan refuses to freeze a list and names the seed. Substituting a different frame (a fixed grid frame, a different seed) would change the pre-registered sampling rule and is not allowed, because the whole point of the pass is to measure that rule.
rule.no_reselection: after states_frozen.json is written the state list is never edited; a shard that fails is rerun on the same frozen list, and a state whose arms cannot all be judged stays in the report as invalid (never dropped, never padded)
forbidden: the fixed frame grid (frames 400/800/1200): the pilot measured 1/9 = 11.1% discrimination there, i.e. ~909 states for 100 proper
dev seeds 1000-1019 as a state source: the gate needs TRAIN ancestors and dev is development exposure
confirm seeds 61000-61499 and legacy 60000-60199: never read
post-hoc selection of states after seeing their |S|

outer_branch_frame_budget.note: prefix replays are an already-recorded trajectory, not new counterfactual frames; they are reported separately

wall.note: every wall clock here is a contention-observed value on a shared 20-vCPU host; it is a measurement of this run, not a throughput promise

cannot_claim: this is label generation, not capability evidence: no score, no clear rate, no dev/confirm evaluation and no generalisation measurement comes out of it
G420-1 is NOT passed: its passed flag is untouched, and this pass does not run the frozen-student continuation contrast the gate also names
|S| = 18 is not 'all 18 first actions are safe': H=120 is a truncation horizon, and a state 30-120 frames before the death is exactly where a death may sit outside the window
|S| = 0 is not 'this state is unwinnable': it means no candidate survived 120 frames under this continuation at this parked state

the states are diagnostic positions on A0's own recorded TRAIN trajectories; they say nothing about seeds 61000-61499 (never read) and nothing about a different checkpoint (D2/B0 would need its own pass)
the wall clocks are contention-observed values on a shared host, not a performance benchmark
the 100-proper floor being met says the label table is large enough to train on; it does not say training on it will improve the student
